body.working_title: How well do smooth and statsforecast estimate ETS parameters?

body.name: Ivan Svetunkov
body.words: Ivan Svetunkov, ORCID 0000-0001-7826-0281. I am the guarantor and the supervisor of this study.

body.text: How well do smooth and statsforecast estimate the smoothing parameters of ETS models on simulated data, in bias, efficiency and consistency?
Study name ets-param-estimation and the local origin remote chosen by the agent, because the human left both to its judgement; the record is not publishable until a public repository URI is given.

Guarantor of the study is Ivan Svetunkov, who is also the author and maintainer of the smooth package that the study evaluates: a competing interest to declare (human's reply, relayed by the coordinator).

body.definition: smooth 1.2.0, class ES with model ANN, AAN or ANA (lags 1 and 12 for ANA), loss='likelihood', bounds='usual', initial='optimal' (initial states estimated by optimisation).
smooth 1.2.0, class ES with the same model, loss and bounds as smooth optimised but its default initial='backcasting' (initial states set by backcasting).
statsforecast 2.1.1, statsforecast.models.ets_f with a fixed model form (ANN, AAN or ANA; m=12 for ANA), opt_crit='lik', bounds='both', initial states estimated with the smoothing parameters.

Series simulated from ETS in innovations form with Gaussian errors, sigma=1, l0=100, b0=1 and seasonal states 10 sin(2 pi k/12), no burn-in; five settings of smoothing parameters, lengths T in {50,100,250,500}, R=300 replicates per cell.
Mean of (estimate minus true value) over the valid replicates of a cell.
Root mean squared error of the estimates around the true value over the valid replicates of a cell.
Mean absolute error of the estimates around the true value over the valid replicates of a cell.
Innovations ETS with additive error, no trend, no seasonality: y_t = l_{t-1} + e_t, l_t = l_{t-1} + alpha e_t.
Innovations ETS with additive error and additive trend: l_t = l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + alpha e_t, b_t = b_{t-1} + beta e_t.
Innovations ETS with additive error and additive seasonality (m=12): l_t = l_{t-1} + alpha e_t, s_t = s_{t-m} + gamma e_t.
Fixed-seed replicates per cell: each replicate series is simulated once and fitted by all three arms.

body.statement: smooth and statsforecast use the same meaning for alpha, beta and gamma (the innovations-form update of the level, trend and seasonal states that the simulation uses), so their estimates are comparable without conversion.
Both implementations estimate the error scale sigma from the data; the simulation fixes sigma = 1 and the estimators are not told it.

body.text: Season indexing: observation t (1-based) has season index (t-1) mod 12 in the initial seasonal states 10 sin(2 pi k/12), k = 0..11, so the first observation's season is index 0 as the brief states.

Failures are counted, not dropped silently: a fit that raises an error or returns a non-finite estimate is excluded from that cell's bias, RMSE and MAE and counted in failed fits (excluded) and non-finite estimates (excluded). Estimates on a bound are included and counted.

Replicates R=300 per cell. Timing from the exploratory pilots RN1-RN3 (3 replicates, lengths 50 and 500) was about 0.03 s per fit; the full design is 18,000 fits, about 10 minutes, below the 20-minute limit, so R stays at 300.
Seeds: pilots RN1-RN3 used seed 20261111. The confirmatory run uses seed 20261112, so its series are new data for the hypotheses.

Comparability: both use the Gaussian likelihood (smooth loss='likelihood', statsforecast opt_crit='lik'). smooth optimised uses initial='optimal'; statsforecast estimates its initial states with the smoothing parameters (its par vector); smooth backcasting (initial='backcasting') is reported as a separate arm. Bounds: smooth bounds='usual' (alpha, beta, gamma in [0,1], beta <= alpha, gamma <= 1-alpha); statsforecast bounds='both' (box [0.0001, 0.9999] plus the admissible restrictions). Estimates within 1e-4 of a bound are counted as on a bound.

body.statement: For the simulated ETS series of [[TM4]] (ETS(A,N,N), ETS(A,A,N) and ETS(A,N,A) with the settings of the design), the RMSE of each smoothing-parameter estimate from [[TM1]], [[TM2]] and [[TM3]] at T=500 is less than half its RMSE at T=50.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: At every setting, smoothing parameter and series length T in {50, 100, 250, 500}, the RMSE of [[TM3]] is within 10% of the RMSE of [[TM1]] for the same estimate.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: For each of [[TM1]], [[TM2]] and [[TM3]] and each smoothing parameter of the settings in [[TM4]], the absolute bias of the estimate at T=500 is at most 0.02.
body.question: Q1

body.design: Simulated series from [[TM4]]: ETS(A,N,N) with alpha = 0.1 and 0.5; ETS(A,A,N) with (alpha, beta) = (0.3, 0.05) and (0.5, 0.2); ETS(A,N,A) with m=12 and (alpha, gamma) = (0.2, 0.1); sigma = 1, Gaussian; l0 = 100, b0 = 1, seasonal states 10 sin(2 pi k/12). T in {50, 100, 250, 500}; R = 300 replicates per cell with seed 20261112. Each replicate series is fitted by smooth optimised, smooth backcasting and statsforecast optimised (fixed model form, no model selection). Script: claimset-code/ets-param-estimation/simulate_fit.py, run with --reps 300 --lengths 50 100 250 500.
body.analysis: Per cell: bias, RMSE and MAE of each estimate around the true value over valid fits; failed and non-finite fits counted and excluded from these, estimates on a bound counted and included. H1: count of (arm, setting, parameter) combinations where the RMSE at T=500 is at least 0.5 times the RMSE at T=50 (H1 violations). H2: count of (setting, parameter, T) combinations where the RMSE ratio of statsforecast optimised to smooth optimised lies outside [0.9, 1.1] (H2 violations). H3: count of (arm, setting, parameter) combinations where |bias| at T=500 exceeds 0.02 (H3 violations).
body.new_data: Series with seed 20261112; the exploratory pilots RN1-RN3 used seed 20261111 and were for timing and checks only.

exclusions.name: failed_fits
exclusions.rule: fits that raise an error or return a non-finite estimate

parameters.sample: 300 replicates per cell, 5 settings x 4 lengths x 3 arms, seed 20261112; no interim analysis; one run

The guard hook and the sudo append-only protection are for the human to decide (claimset-lab skill: the guard restricts the harness, and protection needs an administrator); the human has no administrator step to take yet, and the record has no public remote to anchor to. Q2, a stray question with no hypothesis attached, is left as it is: it is not reported by any paper, and a correction would only add an event.

body.rationale: Rule of PL1: H1 violations = 2, which is neither 0 (supported) nor at least 12 (not supported).
Rule of PL1: H2 violations = 12, which is neither 0 (supported) nor at least 16 (not supported).
Rule of PL1: H3 violations = 3, which is neither 0 (supported) nor at least 12 (not supported).
